source_caption:
The moment they realize they have fallen in love in In the Mood for Love is devastating because nothing dramatic happens. Wong Kar-wai lets the truth appear in silence — in the way Tony Leung and Maggie Cheung stop pretending this is only about their spouses, and suddenly understand that the real danger is what they feel for each other.

In the Mood for Love (2000), directed by Wong Kar-wai, starring Tony Leung, Maggie Cheung, Rebecca Pan. A haunting and exquisitely restrained romance about longing, loneliness, and impossible desire, capturing two people trapped between emotional intimacy and the rules of the world around them.

source_details.title: In the Mood for Love
source_details.synopsis: In the Mood for Love (traditional Chinese: 花樣年華; simplified Chinese: 花样年华; lit. 'Flower-like Years', 'the prime of one's youth') is a 2000 romantic drama film written, directed, and produced by Wong Kar-wai. An international co-production between Hong Kong and France, the film follows a man (Tony Leung) and a woman (Maggie Cheung) in 1962 who discover that their spouses are having an affair. As they spend time together, they gradually develop feelings for one another. It is the second installment in an informal trilogy, preceded by Days of Being Wild (1990) and followed by 2046 (2004). The film premiered in the official competition at the 53rd Cannes Film Festival, where it received acclaim.
